a2c2024: composes decision stages for accuracy; we show that the composition, not the summary statistic, decides whether an added stage pays.
abstainfair2023: makes abstaining classifiers fair; fairness is orthogonal to the composition question this paper isolates.
abstainrank2025: places bounded abstention inside a pairwise ranker; the added layer's marginal catch is the quantity we measure.
aniso2026: trades privacy against utility in a local differential-privacy mechanism; a different trade-off with the same structure of one layer added to another.
ask2025: decides when to require human feedback; asking is our added layer, and we measure the marginal catch it earns.
avizienis1985nversion: builds independent implementations for fault tolerance; we ask when the Nth version repays its capacity.
bacchelli2013codereview: studies what code review expects and what it finds; we treat review as a layer and ask when a second check pays.
bai2022constitutional: uses AI feedback to steer a model towards harmlessness; the feedback layer's value against the base model is what we quantify.
bainbridge1983ironies: explains why automation degrades the operator's skill; we price the layer meant to catch what the automation missed.
benjamini1995fdr: controls the false discovery rate across many tests; we use it where many grid cells are screened.
bmc2026: uses LLM agents for model checking; a checking agent is an added layer, and its marginal catch is what we measure.
branchynet2016: adds early-exit branches to a network; a branch is an added layer, and we price its catches.

breiman2001forests: builds an ensemble whose strength is chiefly empirical; we ask what one added member is worth at fixed accuracy.
calibrateddefer2022: improves the calibration of the deferral score; calibration is necessary but not sufficient here, since equal calibration can accompany different composition.
castro1999pbft: makes Byzantine replication practical; replication is redundancy under an independence assumption our construct measures.
causaldefer2024: gives a causal framework for evaluating a deferring system; we evaluate the marginal effect of adding one, which a whole-system evaluation averages away.
causalperception2024: models perception within a causal framework; we isolate composition with a dial rather than with a model.
cerberus2026: co-designs error-correcting codes across hardware layers; our layers are decision layers, and the dial is where their errors fall, not how they are encoded.
chilgrader2026: calibrates a human-in-the-loop short-answer grading layer; calibration sharpens the score without settling whether the layer pays.
chow1970reject: gives the optimal abstention threshold for a single classifier; we hold a layer's accuracy fixed and ask whether adding it is worth the capacity, not where one model should stop.
closedloop2022: designs closed human-in-the-loop deferral pipelines end to end; we hold the pipeline fixed and vary the placement of the added layer's catches.
cobbe2021verifiers: trains verifiers that raise math accuracy; our break-even states when the verifier beats more of the generator.
complement2022: trains a model to complement a human's decisions; we ask whether that complementarity repays the capacity it takes from the primary.
confidadptive2022: exits a language model early to save compute; we compare that saved compute with a layer that catches errors.
coverage2024: enforces a coverage constraint on human-AI cooperation; we show equal coverage and equal accuracy can still be worth different amounts.
deceptionensembles2019: uses ensemble diversity as a defence against deception; our dial is the constructive version of the same lever.
deepensembles2016: improves predictive uncertainty by ensembling; we show uncertainty summaries can be identical while downstream worth is not.
deferpopulation2024: meta-learns deferral to a population of experts; that population is a single layer in our terms, and we price it against the primary.
deferredseg2026: defers medical image segmentation among experts; the domain is not what governs the marginal value in our results.
dexdeepfm2021: adds diversity to factorisation machines for recommendation; we price diversity where one layer follows another.
dietterich2000ensemble: classifies ensembles by how they are constructed; we classify them by what their errors are worth to the layer already in place.
dietvorst2015aversion: explains why people abandon algorithms after seeing them err; the residual catch is the quantity that makes that abandonment rational or not.
eckhardt1985coincident: analyses multiversion software subject to correlated faults; we show correlation alone does not fix the marginal value.
efron1979bootstrap: introduces resampling for standard errors; we use it to put intervals on the rank correlations and margins the law reports.
exemplars2021: teaches humans when to defer to a classifier; we measure the layer's marginal catch on the primary's wrongness instead of the human's learned policy.
failfast2025: uses deferral to patch the deficiencies of reasoning models; we ask whether that patch beats spending the same capacity on the model.
faircoop2026: optimises fairness in human-AI cooperation on medical images; we hold the layer's accuracy fixed and measure marginal value instead.
fatigue2026: models expert fatigue in a constrained deferral objective; our dial abstracts human cost away to isolate error composition.
fawcett2006roc: summarises a detector by its ranking curve; we show two configurations with the same summary can differ in downstream worth, which no curve read off one layer can express.
feat2025: builds a multi-agent forensic system on domain-adapted LLMs; agent count is redundancy, and we ask what the additional agent adds.
fifar2023: contributes a fraud-detection benchmark for learning to defer; we calibrate on published systems and report the span of the break-even across them.
flowbyflow2026: governs AI output by bypassing content judgment in high-stakes settings; the bypass is an added layer and we price it.
freund1997boosting: bounds boosting's error under weak learners; the catch rate on the primary's errors is exactly what that bound takes as given.
gnnensembles2023: delivers calibrated uncertainty from interatomic-potential ensembles; calibration and marginal value come apart in our results.
guideexperts2023: uses a personalised model to guide human experts; a guiding layer is not a checking layer, and we measure the checking layer against residual errors.
helios2026: drives indirect trajectory optimisation with an LLM agent; we ask when such an additional agent repays its capacity.
heteroens2025: proposes a heterogeneous ensemble as a universal uncertainty metric; a better metric does not settle whether the member repaid its capacity.
hinton1999product: multiplies expert distributions so errors cancel; we isolate that cancellation by reallocating catches at fixed accuracy.
howard1966valueinfo: prices information before it is acquired; our break-even is the same calculus applied to a supervisor's catches.
huang2023selfcorrect: documents that models cannot yet self-correct reasoning unaided; we give the condition under which a correction layer earns its capacity.
identityfree2025: defers to experts not seen in training; we take the layer's identity and accuracy as given and ask what it buys.
jacobs1991mixture: divides labour among local experts through a gating network; our dial divides where each expert's errors fall.
jiang2018trust: scores individual instances for trust; we condition the layer's value on the population the primary got wrong (the residual catch), not on the instance's apparent difficulty.
knight1986nversion: tests whether version failures are independent; that assumption is what our residual catch replaces with a measurement.
knowdefer2025: applies selective prediction to responsible knowledge use; our layer is priced by its catch on the primary's errors.
kuncheva2003diversity: relates ensemble diversity measures to accuracy; we relate the placement of errors to the decision to add a layer at all.
l2dclinical2026: selects a model adaptively in a clinical pipeline; we price the second model against the first rather than choosing among them.
lamport1982byzantine: gives the agreement problem under arbitrary faults; we study a two-layer cascade with correlated failures rather than a consensus protocol.
layered2026: argues for layered supervision in AI-assisted review; we give the condition under which the extra layer pays, and the break-even that sets it.
lecun2015deeplearning: surveys deep learning's methods and prospects; our manuscript prices one component of such systems.
leesee2004trust: states design principles for appropriate reliance on automation; our dial turns the reliance decision into a measurable quantity.
lightman2023verify: shows process supervision improves reasoning; we measure the verifier's marginal catch on the primary's wrong outputs.
limitedexpert2023: works around scarce expert predictions; our binding constraint is capacity rather than labels.
littlewood1989coincident: models coincident failures of redundant software; our dial is the controlled version of that correlation.
liu2023lostmiddle: finds position effects in long-context use; the placement of information is a composition effect of the same kind as the placement of a layer's catches.
ltauf2024: derives uncertainty from training loss trajectories; a different summary of the same errors, which our result shows is not decisive.
ltd2026: traces algorithmic to human bias in learned deferral; we separate bias from composition by holding accuracy fixed.
lyons1962tmr: uses majority voting for reliability; TMR assumes independence, which our dial relaxes explicitly.
madaan2023selfrefine: iterates refinement with self-feedback; the iteration is an added layer and we ask what it is worth at fixed accuracy.
metacog2026: meta-learns a policy for collaborating with humans; that collaboration decision is our break-even.
mllmunc2026: makes multimodal LLM decisions uncertainty-aware; uncertainty is one summary of a layer's errors and does not by itself settle its value.
mozannar2020defer: characterises the Bayes-optimal rule for deferring to an expert; we keep the rule fixed and ask when the deferral capacity is better spent improving the primary.
multidefer2024: post-processes a trained multi-objective deferrer; we hold the layer fixed and move where its catches land.
negcorr2020: shapes member correlation during training; we vary correlation after training with accuracy held fixed.
neuroformal2026: pairs neural generation with symbolic validation of formal functions; that pairing is a deliberately uncorrelated layer, and our dial explains when it pays.
nodefer2025: removes training from the deferral rule; we remove the assumption that the rule's accuracy determines its value.
oodunc2024: uses uncertainty to characterise out-of-distribution inputs; distribution shift moves the residual catch, which is what our law reads.
opv2025: builds an efficient outcome-based process verifier; efficiency changes the cost side of our break-even, not its form.
parasuraman1997automationbias: gives a taxonomy of reliance failures; we give the break-even that separates use from disuse.
partialdefer2025: partially defers over a sequence; the granularity of deferral is not what our dial varies, which is the composition of the layer's errors.
peng2023copilot: measures productivity effects of an AI assistant; we ask whether the supervision of its output repays its cost.
popdemos2025: defers to a population from limited demonstrations; capacity rather than demonstrations is our binding constraint.
psychmachines2026: studies how people learn from machine feedback; we study when the machine's feedback layer is worth its capacity.
querycontrol2025: controls the expert-query budget in active imitation learning; we compare that budget with spending it on the primary.
randell1975faulttolerance: defines the recovery-block structure; we price the added block.
rashomon2025: characterises the set of near-equally-good concept models; our two configurations are precisely such a set, with different downstream worth.
recoveryblocks1985: pairs an acceptance test with a backup block; the backup is an added layer whose residual catch is set by its acceptance test.
reviewerconfidence2025: audits whether reviewer confidence matches review content; confidence is one summary, and summaries do not fix worth.
russell1991metareasoning: decides how much computation to spend thinking; we decide whether to add a thinker, with the primary's errors as the population.
sadowski2018googlereview: describes modern code review practice at Google; we quantify the marginal value of adding a reviewer.
sampleefficient2022: reduces the labels needed to learn human-complementary predictors; we take the learned layer as given and price it.
selectivegeifman2017: learns when a classifier should abstain under a risk target; we take the abstaining layer as given and price it against spending the same capacity on the primary.
selectivenet2019: makes abstention differentiable inside one model; we treat the added check as an option whose value is set by the primary's error population.
seqdefer2021: defers sequential clinical decisions to a human; we analyse one added layer's marginal catch across a calibrated population of published systems rather than one pipeline.
shazeer2017moe: routes tokens to experts to raise capacity; our question is when an extra expert repays its share of that capacity.
shinn2023reflexion: reinforces an agent verbally across attempts; the redundancy is implicit, where ours is a dial.
socdefer2025: applies deferral to alert triage in security operations; our result is methodological, about why an added check helps, rather than a further application.
specgen2026: measures how well LLMs generate formal specifications; generation quality is a summary, and our result is that summaries do not fix worth.
triage2021: triages among models with different costs; our dial holds accuracy fixed, isolating where catches fall from how many there are.
unbiaseddeferral2021: optimises which of several experts receives a case; we reallocate where a fixed-accuracy layer's catches fall and show the choice changes what it is worth.
uncertaintydefer2021: uses predictive uncertainty as the defer signal; we show uncertainty-style summaries can be identical while the layer's worth is not.
unequalunc2025: shows uncertainty is unevenly distributed across groups; that unevenness is one face of the composition effect we formalise.
uqsurvey2023: surveys uncertainty estimation as a trust signal; we show such summaries can be identical while worth differs.
uqvsdefer2025: compares uncertainty quantification with learned deferral as signals; we compare adding a layer with not adding one.
vaswani2017attention: introduces the transformer architecture; we ask whether an additional verification pass over its outputs repays the capacity it takes.
viola2001cascade: builds a boosted cascade tuned for speed and false positives; we make the value of an added cascade stage the object of study.
vlgenrm2025: applies generative reward models to vision-language verification; the modality is not what decides the marginal value.
vqaabstain2022: abstains to avoid incorrect visual answers; our unit is a layer's marginal catch, not one model's decision to answer.
wang2023selfconsistency: samples several reasoning paths and takes a vote; that is internal redundancy, and our dial makes the redeployment explicit and priced.
wei2022cot: elicits multi-step reasoning by prompting; we ask when a second check on that reasoning pays.
wilson1927probable: gives an interval for a binomial proportion; we use it for the calibrated held-out cells.
wolpert1992stacked: learns a combiner over base models; we ask whether the combiner's capacity was better spent strengthening a single model.
workload2024: makes deferral cost-sensitive to expert workload; our budget is the primary's capacity, so the trade-off we study is reallocation.
yao2022react: interleaves reasoning with acting; verifying an action is an added layer whose marginal catch matters.
yao2023tree: searches over intermediate thoughts; search multiplies checks, and we price that multiplication.
zheng2023judge: shows LLM judges correlate with human preferences; we ask when the judge's verdict adds to the first pass rather than repeating it.
